children: Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures fell on Wednesday in a profit-taking retreat after hitting a one-month high in the previous session as accelerating inflation and equities market losses this week stoked concerns about beef demand.
Feeder cattle futures followed live cattle lower.

"Monday we were feeling pretty good about the stocks having found a bottom, demand being good, and everything's fine. But today we're really kind of taking that away," said Ted Seifried, chief market strategist at Zaner Ag Hedge.
Restaurant traffic and retail purchases of beef can slow when consumers are worried about inflation and the broader economy.
The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq retreated on Wednesday amid a tech selloff before paring losses, while the Dow rebounded from earlier declines. The Nasdaq had been down more than 4% earlier in the day.
Inflation increased in October, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027.

The US Department of Agriculture on Tuesday said the US frozen beef supply on October 31 was up 5% from a month earlier and up 2% from a year ago, even as cattle marketings declined in the month. The data suggested beef demand has slowed, analysts said.
The choice boxed beef cutout fell $3.32 on Wednesday to $356.59 per hundredweight, while the select cutout shed $1.29 to $344.71 per cwt, according to the USDA.
ended the day down 2.850 cents at 226.975 cents per pound. CME January feeder cattle
fell 5.375 cents to settle at 327.525 cents per pound.
CME lean hog futures continued a recent slide under pressure from weak demand.
The pork carcass cutout value fell to its lowest point since August 2020 on Tuesday, but was up 74 cents on Wednesday at $66.98 per cwt, USDA data showed.
Most-active February hogs (LHG27) settled a penny lower at 55.425 cents per pound.
